sections.name: DTO Input Validation & Constraint Hardening (HIPAA / DPDP) (part 1)
sections.title: Vital signs and doctor note checks
sections.what: Tests that a valid blood pressure reading and a valid doctor note pass the input checks. It also checks that a negative reading and an unknown vital type are refused.
sections.why: Likely reason: the describe title names HIPAA and DPDP, the health-data privacy rules, so these tests protect the rule that health records must be valid before they are stored.
sections.watch_out: If a rule is loosened on purpose, these tests will fail, so update them with the change rather than deleting them.

sections.name: DTO Input Validation & Constraint Hardening (HIPAA / DPDP) (part 2)
sections.title: Patient ID and date checks
sections.what: Tests that a doctor note with a patient ID that is not a valid ID is refused, and that a follow-up date that is not a real date is refused. It also checks that a symptom accepts a list of text triggers and refuses a list of numbers.
sections.why: Likely reason: stops broken references and malformed lists from reaching the database.

sections.name: DTO Input Validation & Constraint Hardening (HIPAA / DPDP) (part 3)
sections.title: User profile and doctor share checks
sections.what: Tests that a profile update with a valid birth date, gender, and blood group passes, and that a bad birth date or unknown gender is refused. It also checks that a chat message needs a valid session ID and that a doctor share lasts between 1 and 90 days.
sections.why: Likely reason: the 90-day limit caps how long a doctor can see a patient's records, and the other checks keep profile data clean.
sections.watch_out: The 90-day limit is written into these tests, so a change to the limit in the code must be matched here or the tests fail.
